title: A Systematic Literature Review on LLM Defenses Against Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking: Expanding NIST Taxonomy
explain_beginner: Large language models like ChatGPT can be tricked by carefully written prompts that make them leak secrets, perform unauthorized tasks, or give false information. Researchers reviewed 88 studies on ways to protect against these attacks and organized their findings using a framework from the US government agency NIST. The work identifies different defense strategies, measures how well each one works with different models, and creates a practical guide for developers building safer AI systems.
explain_business: Organizations deploying large language models face significant security risks from prompt injection attacks that can cause data breaches or system misuse. This research catalogs proven defense strategies with measured effectiveness across different models, enabling technical teams to select appropriate protections based on their specific systems and threat profiles. The standardized framework and open-source solutions identified help companies implement defenses efficiently while reducing security vulnerabilities and potential liability from AI system compromise.
explain_practitioner: This systematic review analyzed 88 peer-reviewed studies on prompt injection defenses and extended NIST's adversarial machine learning taxonomy with additional defense categories. The authors documented quantitative effectiveness metrics for mitigation strategies across specific LLMs and attack datasets, cataloguing which defenses are open-source and model-agnostic. By establishing standardized terminology and taxonomy grounded in NIST's framework, the work provides a structured foundation for comparing defense mechanisms and enables reproducible research for developing more robust LLM security solutions.
